title: Household Task Backlog Burn-Down
dataSources: Baby feeds (`baby:feed`), baby sleep (`baby:sleep`), diaper changes (`diaper:change`), chore completions (`chore:completion`), allowance ledger (`allowance:ledger`), family calendar (`family:calendar`), growth measurements (`growth:measurement`).
app: Baby-tracking apps (Huckleberry/Baby Daybook exports), chore and allowance boards, shared family calendars, and growth logs — sent to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=chore:completion
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(eval(if(status="added",1,0))) as added, sum(eval(if(status="done",1,0))) as done by _time
| streamstats sum(added) as total_added, sum(done) as total_done
| eval backlog=total_added-total_done
| sort - _time
description: Tracks the household to-do backlog rising and falling over time, treating home chores like a project sprint.
value: A growing backlog is the early sign the household is falling behind; a burn-down makes it visible before the clutter wins.
implementation: Log task additions and completions into `index=personal`; schedule daily and trend the open backlog.
visualization: Area chart of household task backlog over time.
grandmaExplanation: It shows whether the household to-do list is growing or shrinking, so chores never quietly pile up.
